name: Sheet row to XRechnung, sent by email (invowerk)

parameters.content:
## Sheet row to XRechnung by email
Each new row in your invoice sheet becomes an XRechnung (UBL XML), checked against the EN 16931 and XRechnung rules by invowerk, and is emailed to the buyer as an attachment.

### Setup
1. Install the community node `@invowerk-dev/n8n-nodes-invowerk`.
2. Get an API key: https://invowerk.dev/go/tpl-zeile-zu-xrechnung?to=/app/api-keys
3. Create the sheet with these header columns: `invoice_number`, `issue_date`, `due_date`, `buyer_reference`, `buyer_name`, `buyer_city`, `buyer_post_code`, `buyer_country`, `buyer_email`, `item`, `quantity`, `unit_price`, `vat_rate`.
4. Pick the sheet in **New invoice row**, edit `SELLER` in **Build invoice body**, connect Gmail.

The trigger carries one pinned sample row: run the workflow once (without the email step) to see the result.

### Your figures
The code computes quantity x price and the VAT for one line at one rate. invowerk does not recompute amounts: it writes them into the XML and rejects an invoice that breaks a rule. XRechnung needs a buyer reference (Leitweg-ID for public buyers).

### invowerk: Generate Invoice
Flavor `xrechnung`, syntax `ubl`. invowerk checks the XML it built; an invoice that breaks a rule is never returned, the node fails instead.
